question:
I'm currently using DBT for transformations from a large CSV file that's received every day that we load into our data warehouse. Unfortunately, the CSV file is sent to us by a vendor and they're unable to sent diffs so we get the full file every day (the file should never have rows deleted/only added). We had an issue recently where something happened on their end and the file we received somehow had rows deleted which caused downstream issues.

Is there a way in dbt to add a test that would make sure that a table always has has >= to the number of rows its had historically?
title: Using dbt to Test that Table Continues to Get Larger Over Time
answer:
In dbt projects, creating a base table, such as base_vendor__model, is recommended for performing complex operations before staging your data.

To ensure consistency in your data flow, you can implement a singular test that verify the new table consistently contains additional records.

An example test can be:

SELECT id 
FROM {{ref('base_vendor__model')}}
WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM {{ref('stg_vendor_table')}})

This test will fail if any ID present in the staging table (your previous day's table) is absent in the base table (the recently fetched data).

Utilize the dbt build command to trigger the creation of a new model, like stg_vendor__model.sql, solely upon the successful completion of this test:

SELECT * FROM {{ ref('base_model_sql')}}

For more detailed information and best practices on structuring dbt projects, refer to this resource.
